title: Database model (database.json)
description: The DATABASE MODEL: the schema model of one database PLUS its per-column filterable surface — "what can be filtered in this database". A property of the database itself, identical across audits, computed ONCE at database indexing by a read-only profiler (the salvaged PR #152 profiler, folded into this model). Renamed from the old database.md. PURELY REGENERABLE — re-index rebuilds it wholesale from the live schema; it carries no user-set state (contrast audit.json, mapping-artifact-redesign.md §6). The values/range it records are the choice domain (what a filter COULD be set to), a HINT not authority: the authoritative cohort number is always a live COUNT (§5).

schema_version.description: Schema version of this document. Required so consumers can migrate. Currently always "1".

status.description: Operational indexing-lifecycle state of this entity — NOT part of the database's content, but carried in-model so there is no separate status sidecar (one file per entity). "indexing" while the model is being built (a stub document, tables may be empty), "ready" once a validated model is written, "error" if the build failed. Optional — an absent status is treated as "ready".

error.description: Human-readable failure reason, present only when status is "error". Optional.

database.description: Stable slug identifying the database (e.g. "cord-ph"). Matches the var/databases/<database_id>/ folder. Required — the primary key for the database.

title.description: Human-readable database title shown in the library (e.g. "Cord pH EMR"). Required.

description.description: One-paragraph prose model of the database: which tables hold what, the primary entity, and where free-text lives. Fed to the LLM as orientation and surfaced in the library (D6). Required.

summary.description: A one-line, ~5–10 word plain-English summary of what the database contains (e.g. "Maternity & neonatal birth records with cord-blood gases"). Shown as the database one-liner in the Library audit-detail page's Databases section. Optional — when absent the UI falls back to the first sentence of `description`.

identity_links.description: MEASURED cross-database identity links: which of this database's identifier columns hold the same values as a column in a SIBLING database. Computed deterministically at indexing time by value-overlap sampling (profile.discover_identity_links) — never written by the LLM. The mapping reads these as facts when deciding identity.keys, and the compiled A3 identity bridge rests on them. Optional — absent when the database was indexed without siblings or no link was measured. Within-database FKs are recorded separately in `foreign_keys`, measured the same way.

target.description: The sibling column holding the same identity values, as "<database_id> -> <table>.<column>" (e.g. "npda-demographics -> patients.nhs_number").

evidence.description: The measurement that proved the link (e.g. "24/24 sampled values found in target").

foreign_keys.description: MEASURED within-database foreign keys: which of this database's columns hold values drawn from another table's key column in the SAME database. Computed deterministically at indexing by value-overlap containment (profile.discover_foreign_keys), unioned with any declared SQL constraints (PRAGMA foreign_key_list) — never written by the LLM. The mapping reads these as facts when authoring criteria_bindings[].join_path, and the populate compiler follows them to emit multi-hop within-database JOINs (Tier-1 try_direct). Distinct from identity_links, which are CROSS-database. Optional — absent when no within-database FK was measured.

column.description: The FK-bearing column, as "<table>.<column>" (e.g. "registrations.patient_id"). No "<db> ->" prefix — unambiguous within one model.

target.description: The referenced key column in the SAME database, as "<table>.<column>" (e.g. "patients.patient_id"). Same field name as identity_links.target for consistent wording across cross-db bridges and within-db join hops.

cardinality.description: Fan-out of the join FROM the referenced key TO the FK-bearing table: "to-one" when the FK column is all-distinct (one row per key — a safe direct multi-hop JOIN), "to-many" when it repeats (a join would fan out; Tier-1 cannot pick a single value and must delegate the field to the agent). The constraint is per-hop in the direction traversed, not that the whole relationship is 1:1.

declared.description: true when the edge comes from a real SQL constraint (PRAGMA foreign_key_list): certain, carries no evidence. false when MEASURED by value-overlap. On conflict, declared wins.

evidence.description: The measurement that proved a MEASURED link (e.g. "10/10 sampled values found in target"). Required when declared is false; absent when declared is true.

allOf.description: A measured FK must carry its measurement; a declared FK must not.

conventions.description: Database-wide rules across tables. Optional — absent/empty on clean databases (e.g. current synthetic fixtures). Two deliberately separated kinds: `row_filters` are EXECUTABLE (the Tier-1 compiler ANDs them into emitted JOINs); `notes` are ORIENTATION prose only. ASSERTED (LLM/human), never measured — DURABLE across re-index, never recomputed wholesale.

row_filters.description: Per-table predicates the compiler MUST AND into any SQL reading the table (soft-delete "deleted_at IS NULL", SCD2 "valid_to IS NULL"), so multi-hop direct JOINs never pull deleted/superseded rows.

predicate.description: A boolean SQL expression referencing ONLY columns of this row_filter's `table` (e.g. "deleted_at IS NULL", "status != 'void' AND valid_to IS NULL"). Columns may be written bare or already table-qualified; the compiler alias-qualifies every bare column when ANDing the predicate into an emitted JOIN.

notes.description: Free-form orientation bullets true database-wide but NOT executable ("All timestamps are UTC", "Amounts are integer cents", "legacy_* tables are frozen"). Surfaced in the lookup digest and mapping prompt; never compiled to SQL.

schema_fingerprint.description: Hash of the database STRUCTURE — table names, each table's column names+types, and the foreign_keys + identity_links edges. Lets re-index trigger on drift (not on a schedule) and lets runtime assert the model matches the live DB before trusting it. Deterministic. Optional (back-compat), recommended.

tables.description: One record per table in the database. Required. Each carries the table's role and its columns (with the filterable surface annotations). Identifier/free-text/reference columns are still listed (with filterable:false + a reason) so the model is complete.

name.description: The table name as it appears in the database (e.g. "cord_ph_birth_records"). Required.

row_count.description: Number of rows at profiling time. Optional — a hint for the LLM and the library; not authoritative (re-profile on demand).

grain.description: Prose statement of what one row represents (e.g. "one row per patient registration"). Always populated: the deterministic all-distinct-key SIGNAL is the floor (one-row-per-entity when the table has an all-distinct identifier column, else an event/measurement table — many per entity), refined into clearer prose by the LLM when it indexes. Optional in the contract for back-compat; when absent the catalog/digest falls back to the first sentence of `description`. DURABLE: preserved across re-index (merged by table name), re-derived only when the table fingerprint changes.

fingerprint.description: Hash of THIS table's structure — its column names+types and the FK edges touching it. Enables the durable-semantics merge to preserve asserted fields (description, grain) when the table is structurally unchanged, re-deriving them only when this changes. Optional.

description.description: Prose role of the table (e.g. "One row per baby / birth record — the audit's primary entity."). Required — orients mapping and identity decisions.

columns.description: One record per column. Required. Carries the column's type, description, and its filterable-surface annotations.

name.description: The column name as stored (e.g. "delivery"). Required.

type.description: The column's storage type as profiled (e.g. "text", "integer", "real", "date"). Required — the raw type from schema introspection, distinct from filter_type which is the meaningful filtering type.

description.description: Prose meaning of the column (e.g. "Mode of delivery."). Required — the library (D6) surfaces this directly and mapping uses it to bind audit concepts.

filterable.description: Whether this column is meaningfully filterable. Required and TYPE-BASED / audit-independent: true for a real category/date/number; false for identifiers, free-text, and references. Never min/max an ID, never enumerate an identifier as a category, never list a free-text column.

filter_type.description: How the column is filtered when filterable:true — "category" (a bounded set, see values), "number" or "date" (a range, see range). Required when filterable is true; absent when filterable is false.

values.description: The choice domain for a category filter: the bounded set of observed values (e.g. ["Spontaneous vaginal","Emergency caesarean",...]). A HINT, not authority — re-profile on demand. Present for filter_type "category".

range.description: The choice domain for a number/date filter: the observed bounds. A HINT, not authority. Present for filter_type "number" or "date".

min.description: Lower bound of the observed range (number for filter_type number; ISO date string for date).

max.description: Upper bound of the observed range (number for filter_type number; ISO date string for date).

codes.description: For a coded DB column: a code -> meaning map of how this database encodes the column's values. Optional. The mapping's per-field `code` bridges the audit's permitted_values to these database codes; E2 cross-checks the two.

reason.description: Why the column is NOT filterable. Required when filterable is false; absent when true. One of: "identifier" (a key/id), "free-text" (unbounded prose), "reference" (a code/foreign-key reference column).

allOf.description: A filterable column must declare HOW it is filtered.
A non-filterable column must declare WHY (and carries no filter_type).
